newsitem.title: USA: Heavy rain to fall in US Midwest through Friday.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rain to fall in US Midwest through Friday.

text.p: Heavy rain fell late Wednesday in Missouri and Arkansas and more is forecast for the next 24 hours from eastern Texas to Ohio, with amounts ranging from 1/2 to three inches, meteorologists said.
"Anywhere that is getting two inches of rain is shut down from harvesting crops for at least several days," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp agriculture meteorologist.

Eastern Missouri to Arkansas received two to five inches of rain late Wednesday prompting flash flood warnings. More rain was forecast there Thursday, with storms clearing out Friday, said Tim Bowden, Weather Express Inc meterologist.
Most of the rain will be concentrated in eastern Midwest, with light scattered showers likely Thursday and Friday in Iowa, southern Minnesota and northwest Illinois.
As cold weather enters the Midwest late Friday some of the rain could turn to snow in the northern and eastern Midwest, but no significant snow amounts were expected.
It will turn cold Friday, with low temperatures dipping into the teens to mid-20s Fahrenheit across northern Illinois to Ohio. Highs should range from the mid-30s to mid-40s.
Burgio said high winds could be associated with the advancing storm systems.
Most of the High Plains, from Nebraska to central Texas, remained dry Thursday and should be dry through most of next week, allowing for harvest to advance, said Bowden.
